articles.title: Mumbai Port's Jawahar Dweep Becomes India's First Plastic-Free Oil Terminal - Swarajya
articles.content: Oct 03, 2026 | Updated 08:56 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Mumbai Port Authority declared its Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal plastic-free yesterday (2 October), marking a significant environmental milestone for India's maritime sector. The offshore facility becomes the country's first oil terminal to completely eliminate single-use plastics, with the announcement made during the Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 cleanliness programme held to mark Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary. The island terminal, also known as Butcher Island, consists of five berths handling crude oil and petroleum products approximately four kilometres off Mumbai's coast. The facility serves major refineries including BPCL, HPCL, IOCL, and ONGC, and petroleum cargo accounts for nearly three-fifths of Mumbai Port's overall traffic. Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal addressed the achievement at the programme, stating that a plastic-free Jawahar Dweep demonstrates India's ports can maintain growth whilst preserving environmental standards. He also dedicated new Oil Spill Response facilities to the nation during the event. The Mumbai Port Authority banned single-use plastics across its premises from September 2021, following the Prime Minister's national call to curb plastic pollution. The port authority has now committed to extending similar measures across its docks, residential colonies, and coastal areas throughout the remainder of the year. articles.title: Vande Bharat sets 100 kmph record over Chenab Bridge | Daily Pioneer
articles.content: October 03, 2026 Vande Bharat sets 100 kmph record over Chenab Bridge Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday announced that Vande Bharat Express has set a new record by crossing the world’s highest railway bridge, the Chenab Bridge, and India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge, the Anji Bridge, at 100 km/h on the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL). In a post on X, the Railways Minister shared a video of Vande Bharat Express crossing the Chenab bridge. “100 km/h over India’s engineering pride”, wrote the Railways Minister. “The maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph,” Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said in a statement here in Jammu. The upgrade is expected to make train operations on the USBRL smoother, cut travel time, and offer passengers a faster, safer, and more comfortable journey. The 111-km Katra-Banihal section is a crucial and technically challenging component of the USBRL project, which is aimed at providing seamless rail connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of the country. The Railway Ministry approved the enhancement of the maximum permissible speed to 100 kmph after all prescribed safety conditions were complied with by the Railways in August this year, officials said. Earlier, trains were permitted to operate at a maximum speed of 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section. The Katra-Banihal section traverses some of the most difficult and rugged terrain of the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, involving deep valleys, steep mountain slopes, major rivers and highly complex geological formations. The section has some of the country’s most prestigious and challenging engineering structures, including the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world’s highest railway bridge, constructed over the Chenab River near Reasi, and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. The section also has 33 tunnels. Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra on June 6, 2025. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

articles.title: Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges Breaking News Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges By Urban Acres October 3, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Indian Railways has raised the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link from 75 kmph to 100 kmph, after Vande Bharat Express trains successfully completed trials across the Chenab and Anji bridges at the higher speed. The trial was conducted with Vande Bharat Express trains 26401 and 26404. During the run, the trains crossed the Chenab Rail Bridge, described as the world’s highest railway arch bridge, and the Anji Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge, at 100 kmph. The speed enhancement follows the Railways’ clearance of the section after it met the required safety parameters. Earlier, the maximum permissible speed was 85 kmph between Katra and Sangaldan and 75 kmph between Sangaldan and Banihal. The revised limit standardises the maximum permissible speed for the 111-km Katra-Banihal section at 100 kmph, according to the report. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared a video of the trial on X and called the development a historic milestone. The successful run demonstrates the operational use of two of the USBRL project’s most technically significant structures while the railway link continues to connect the Jammu region with the Kashmir Valley. The Chenab Rail Bridge stands 359 metres above the riverbed and spans 1,315 metres. The Anji Bridge rises 331 metres above the riverbed and stretches 725 metres across the valley. Their inclusion in the trial run places the bridges at the centre of the latest operational milestone, rather than treating them only as construction achievements. The Katra-Banihal section is a crucial part of the rail connection between the Jammu region and the Kashmir Valley. The increase in permissible speed is expected to improve operational efficiency, reduce travel time and provide a faster and more comfortable journey for passengers using the route. The development also marks a shift from construction and engineering milestones towards the performance of the completed railway infrastructure in regular operations. The higher speed limit will apply after the Railways’ safety clearance for the section. The latest trial involved the Vande Bharat trains crossing both landmark bridges at 100 kmph, with the revised operating parameters now forming the next stage of the USBRL corridor’s development.
